claims.text: The untreated nearly equiatomic multi-element catalyst suffers activity loss under transient and low-temperature exhaust conditions.
The untreated catalyst has durability limitations under transient and low-temperature exhaust conditions.
A closed-loop high-throughput pipeline can identify synthesis parameters that improve the catalyst.
The proposed pipeline integrates automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated aging, rapid activity screening, and Bayesian optimization.
Machine-learning-guided optimization can fine-tune catalyst composition and processing parameters.
Optimized processing will produce tailored microstructural features and elemental distributions.
Controlled phase segregation or dopant distributions may stabilize active sites.
Tailored microstructure and elemental distributions may inhibit sintering or aggregation of catalytic phases.
Optimized elemental dispersion and microstructure will reduce deactivation caused by sintering or detrimental phase segregation.
Reducing these deactivation mechanisms will improve low-temperature catalytic activity relative to the untreated starting catalyst.
Reducing these deactivation mechanisms will improve durability under thermal and mileage-induced aging relative to the untreated starting catalyst.
The optimized catalyst will maintain low platinum-group-metal usage.
The predicted benefits apply during transient and low-temperature gasoline or hybrid-vehicle exhaust operation involving H2O, NO, and thermal-aging stress.
The approach may not remain effective when other deactivation mechanisms dominate or when relevant synthesis parameters cannot be modified.

The hypothesis is falsified if pipeline optimization fails to produce statistically significant improvements in both low-temperature activity and durability without increasing platinum consumption relative to the control.
